new.n: Sherman Lumber Co. mill, north shore of Half Moon Lake (1881)
new.pl: End of Randall Street, north shore of Half Moon Lake, Eau Claire
new.v: Mill-hand coins and tokens, tools, slab and sawdust fill along the shore
new.st: Arthur and John Sherman built their lumber mill here in 1881, on the north shore of Half Moon Lake at the end of Randall Street, across the water from the Carson Park peninsula. It burned to the ground after two months and was rebuilt the next season. A painting of the mill from about 1885, probably by the Swiss-born travelling artist Frank C. Peyraud (the Eau Claire Daily Leader of September 1885 says he was painting the Sherman mill), is the cover of Pfaff's book; the Sherman sisters kept it over the fireplace at 700 Second Avenue. The Half Moon Lake beach is about 80 m south of this pin today.
new.t: Mill sites leave slab and sawdust fill along the shore; workers' coins and tokens turn up by the old road to the mill. This is city park and beach ground: check the park rules first.

new.n: Old Eau Claire High School, 4th Avenue between Lake Street and Grand Avenue
new.pl: 4th Avenue between Lake Street and West Grand Avenue, Eau Claire
new.v: Coins, class rings, buttons, slate pencils, marbles
new.st: Pfaff (p. 111) shows a Victorian brick high school with a corner tower on 4th Avenue between Lake Street and Grand Avenue; the building is gone today. A 1925 letter from Aunt Mary Walmsley contrasts "the first little schoolhouse" with this "handsome large building". Decades of students passed through it.
new.t: Lawn strips and any unbuilt corner of the block are where old coins and class rings turn up. Ask the current owner first.

new.n: Hotel Eau Claire (1921), Barstow and Eau Claire Streets
new.pl: Corner of Barstow and Eau Claire Streets, downtown Eau Claire
new.st: The "new million dollar fireproof" Hotel Eau Claire opened on Wednesday, 1 June 1921, at the corner of Barstow and Eau Claire Streets, with Joseph P. Dilley as general manager and a modern cafe and coffee shop promising "sudden service" (1921 ad in Pfaff, pp. 106-107). A 1920s Library of Congress photo on the book's back cover shows cars crowding the street in front. On the 1883 Sanborn map the Eau Claire House hotel stood about 25 m from this corner (see that pin), so the corner may have held a hotel for 40 years or more.
new.t: Downtown and paved: mainly a story stop for a historic walk. Look only at boulevard strips, with permission.

d-half-moon-beach.st: In the 1920s, with the log drives over, Half Moon Lake became a popular summer swimming hole (Pfaff, Settlement and Survival, p. 111). The Sherman Lumber Co. mill of 1881 stood about 80 m north of this pin, at the end of Randall Street (see that pin).

d-carson-park.st: Across the water on the north shore, at the end of Randall Street, stood the Sherman Lumber Co. mill (built 1881, burned after two months, rebuilt 1882; see that pin). The "island" was later deeded to the city and named for lumberman William Carson (Pfaff, p. 128).

sf-eau-claire-galloway-house-hotel.st: On 19 October 1916 the Galloway House hosted the downtown banquet for the dedication of the Eau Claire State Normal School, with Governor Emanuel Philipp and Regent Emmet Horan (Pfaff, p. 108, citing the Eau Claire Leader of 20 October 1916).
